newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to overhaul 16 ailing firms.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to overhaul 16 ailing firms.

text.p: The Croatian government decided on Monday to overhaul 16 ailing companies by shifting their debts to state banks and utilities or covering them from the Privatisation Fund portfolio, state televsion reported.
The companies include aluminium producer TLM, shipbuilders and repairers Torpedo, Brodomaterijal and Brodoremont, steelmill Zeljezara Split and ferrous alloy maker Dalmacija.
They employ altogether some 10,500 workers, the majority of whom would retain their jobs after the overhaul, the television reported but did not say when the process would start.
The heavily indebted TLM owes large sums to Splitska Banka, which is currently being overhauled, and to the state customs. The government decided to annul the debt.
TLM's other debts to the state electricity board (HEP) and Zagrebacka banka will be covered by transferring the company's stocks from the portfolio of the state-run Privatisation Fund.
But the company will have to put together some 19 million German marks needed for its restructuring on its own, by attracting foreign partners, the television said.

The government said it would not go beyond settling old debts, and companies would in the future have to fend for themselves, the television said. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
